Stepwise regression

Source: R/blr-stepwise-regression.R
blr_step_p_both.Rd

Build regression model from a set of candidate predictor variables by entering and removing predictors based on p values, in a stepwise manner until there is no variable left to enter or remove any more.

Usage

blr_step_p_both(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
blr_step_p_both(model, pent = 0.1, prem = 0.3, details = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'blr_step_p_both'
plot(x, model = NA, print_plot = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

model

An object of class glm; the model should include all candidate predictor variables. Only binary logistic regression models (binomial family with logit link) are supported. Weighted models (any prior weight other than 1) and grouped binomial models (cbind(successes, failures) or proportions) are not supported; the model must be fitted with model = TRUE, y = TRUE.

...

Other arguments.

pent

p value; variables with p value less than pent will enter into the model.

prem

p value; variables with p more than prem will be removed from the model.

details

Logical; if TRUE, will print the regression result at each step.

x

An object of class blr_step_p_both.

print_plot

logical; if TRUE, prints the plot else returns a plot object.

Value

blr_step_p_both returns an object of class "blr_step_p_both". An object of class "blr_step_p_both" is a list containing the following components:

model

final model; an object of class glm Only binary logistic regression models (binomial family with logit link) are supported. Weighted models (any prior weight other than 1) and grouped binomial models (cbind(successes, failures) or proportions) are not supported; the model must be fitted with model = TRUE, y = TRUE.

orders

candidate predictor variables according to the order by which they were added or removed from the model

method

addition/deletion

steps

total number of steps

predictors

variables retained in the model (after addition)

aic

akaike information criteria

bic

bayesian information criteria

dev

deviance

indvar

predictors

Aliased terms

A model with aliased (perfectly collinear) coefficients is rejected with an error, because the Wald test used to enter or remove terms does not exist for them. Remove the aliased terms and refit.

References

Chatterjee, Samprit and Hadi, Ali. Regression Analysis by Example. 5th ed. N.p.: John Wiley & Sons, 2012. Print.

Examples

# \donttest{
# stepwise regression
model <- glm(y ~ ., data = stepwise, family = binomial(link = 'logit'))
blr_step_p_both(model)
#> Stepwise Selection Method   
#> ---------------------------
#> 
#> Candidate Terms: 
#> 
#> 1. x1 
#> 2. x2 
#> 3. x3 
#> 4. x4 
#> 5. x5 
#> 6. x6 
#> 
#> We are selecting variables based on p value...
#> 
#> Variables Entered/Removed: 
#> 
#> - x6 added 
#> - x1 added 
#> - x3 added 
#> - x2 added 
#> - x6 added 
#> - x5 added 
#> 
#> No more variables to be added/removed.
#> 
#> 
#> Final Model Output 
#> ------------------
#> 
#>                              Model Overview                               
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Data Set    Resp Var     Obs.    Df. Model    Df. Residual    Convergence 
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> stepwise       y        20000        4           19995           TRUE     
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                     Response Summary                     
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> Outcome        Frequency        Outcome        Frequency 
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#>    0             10041             1             9959    
#> --------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>                    Maximum Likelihood Estimates                    
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Parameter     DF    Estimate    Std. Error    z value     Pr(>|z|) 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------
#> (Intercept)    1     -1.5228        0.0287    -53.1302      0.0000 
#>     x1         1      1.0276        0.0212     48.4927      0.0000 
#>     x3         1      1.0260        0.0213     48.2799      0.0000 
#>     x2         1      0.9807        0.0209     46.9690      0.0000 
#>     x5         1      0.0357        0.0192      1.8531      0.0639 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>  Association of Predicted Probabilities and Observed Responses  
#> ---------------------------------------------------------------
#> % Concordant          0.8911          Somers' D        0.7821   
#> % Discordant          0.1089          Gamma            0.7821   
#> % Tied                0.0000          Tau-a            0.3911   
#> Pairs                99998319         c                0.8911   
#> ---------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> 
#>                       Stepwise Selection Summary                       
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#>                      Added/                                                  
#> Step    Variable    Removed        AIC           BIC         Deviance     
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#>    1       x6       addition     18869.627     18885.434    18865.6270    
#>    2       x1       addition     18571.376     18595.087    18565.3760    
#>    3       x3       addition     18016.724     18048.338    18008.7240    
#>    4       x2       addition     16642.374     16681.891    16632.3740    
#>    5       x6       removal      16640.653     16672.267    16632.6530    
#>    6       x5       addition     16639.219     16678.736    16629.2190    
#> ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# stepwise regression plot
model <- glm(y ~ ., data = stepwise, family = binomial(link = 'logit'))
k <- blr_step_p_both(model)
